previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of chronic systolic and diastolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, diabetes, and morbid obesity was admitted for worsening shortness of breath over two days. He presented with symptoms of a viral upper respiratory infection, including congestion, dry cough, chills, and headache, which exacerbated his underlying heart condition. Initial evaluation revealed tachycardia in the 120s-140s due to atrial fibrillation, mild pulmonary vascular congestion on chest X-ray, and an elevated BNP of 1243, though trending downward. He was managed conservatively with continued home medications, including furosemide, metoprolol, warfarin, and insulin, without the need for oxygen or procedural intervention. His symptoms improved, and he was discharged in stable condition with no medication changes, advised to adhere to a low-sodium diet, fluid restriction, and daily weight monitoring.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAM:  Head CT, ___.

COMPARISON:  None.

CLINICAL INFORMATION:  ___ male with left facial droop and left hand
incoordination.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous 5-mm axial images were acquired of the head without the
use of intravenous contrast.

FINDINGS:  There is no evidence of intracranial hemorrhage.  There is no mass
effect or midline shift.  The ventricles and sulci are normal in size and
configuration.  Gray-white differentiation is preserved throughout.  The
visualized orbits and soft tissue structures are unremarkable.  The mastoid
air cells are clear.  There is soft tissue density completely opacifying the
left maxillary sinus, though there is no associated bony thickening of the
maxillary sinus walls.  The frontal, ethmoid, and sphenoid sinuses are clear.
The right maxillary sinus is clear.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No acute intracranial process.
2.  Soft tissue opacification of the left maxillary sinus likely mucoid
impaction.

HISTORY:  Male with dysarthria and weakness, to evaluate for intracranial
pathology.

TECHNIQUE:  Multiplanar MR ___ without contrast; 3D TOF MRA Head without
contrast and GAdo enhanced MRA Neck with reformations. Study, esplly MRA Head
is suboptimal due to pt. motion. 


FINDINGS:

MRI ___:

Multiple foci of restricted diffusion are seen in the right parietal cortex,,
right insular cortex, right temporal lobe and right inferior cerebellar
hemisphere; some of these are not well seen on the ADC images, most likely due
to different chronicity of these.  The alrgest is located in the right
parietal cortex and ___ associated FALIR hyperintens signal. Overall
appearances are most consistent with acute or subacute infarcts(image 4,, 13
and 16, series 10). There is no evidence to suggest a hemorrhagic
transformation.  There is no evidence of  mass effect.  The ventricles and
sulci are normal in size and configuration. There is a large retention
cyst/polyp in the left maxillary sinus along with some mucosla thickening.
Minimal mucosal thickening is noted in the right mastoid air cells.  

MRA HEAD:  

The inferior division of the right Middle cerebral artery is not well seen on
the reformations; however, it is seen on the source images and there is no
flow limitation distally. Hence, the appearance on the reformations, is likely
artifactual related to different orientation of the vessel. This segment is
well seen on the GADO MRA images of the neck. There is slight prominence of
the left MCA, due to confluence of vessels. The rest of the  intracranial,
vertebral and internal carotid arteries and their major branches appear normal
without evidence of significant stenosis, occlusion, or an aneurysm more than
3 mm (within the resolution of MRA). 

MRA NECK: 
The origins of arch vessels are patent. The carotid and vertebral arteries are
visualized from their origins through the intracranial course.  There is no
evidence of flow limting stenosis, occlusion, or an aneurysm.

IMPRESSION:

1. Multiple acute/subacute infarcts, the largest in the right parietal lobe,
insular cortex, right temporal lobe and right inferior cerebellar hemisphere,
likely embolic given the different territories, as described above, the
largest in the right parietal lobe. To corrleate for embolic source.

2. Patent major arteries with details as above without flow limting stenosis,
occlusion, or an aneurysm more than 3mm within the resolution of MRA.

REASON FOR EXAMINATION:  Shortness of breath.
